WHY IT FAILS (airtight, SASS-confirmed on sm_100):
- Plain baseline BIG kernel SASS: 340 ATOMS, 0 MATCH, 0 VOTE. nvcc does NOT auto-aggregate, and R=1 is STILL the champion -> the HW shared-memory ATOMS unit already coalesces the hot bin's 32-way same-address conflict cheaply.

Adding MIO collectives to relieve an MIO bottleneck is self-defeating -> 7.5x slowdown. The brief's premise ('MATCH hides in MIO shadow, sheds 3.2x of the hot bin') is FALSE on Blackwell: MATCH COMPETES for MIO, the HW already aggregates same-address atomics.

GENERALIZATION FOR FUTURE BRIEFS: every hand-written warp-collective anti-contention scheme (warp-agg/match, R-replication, PWARP, bank-rotation -- all now remote-dead) hits the SAME wall: they relocate or pre-combine atomics but issue the SAME-or-MORE MIO-pipe instructions. The kernel's wall is MIO INSTRUCTION THROUGHPUT, and the ATOMS count is irreducible without leaving the per-element-atomic algorithm class. The ONLY remaining lever is to REDUCE THE TOTAL MIO/ATOM INSTRUCTION COUNT via a fundamentally different algorithm -- which is OUTSIDE this brief and which worker-0 independently reached too (they are now trying CUB DeviceHistogram on brief 3, got 16.378 local).
